item.title: BSides Saskatoon: Armouring incident responders
item.description: In this talk, I explored real-world experiences navigating security incident handling in high-stress environments, where customer impacts are real, and where it can feel like someone is always watching over my shoulder and judging my effectiveness. Autonomy is also commonly very low; I am expected to work magic, often without the ability to directly influence root causes and meaningful change. No two incidents are ever the same, and each requires a level of preparation and training I never feel I have enough time for. Due to these complexities, security operations and incident response is one of the highest stress positions in our industry, which is even more scary when I consider it's often the entry point for practitioners into cybersecurity.

item.title: BSides Edmonton: Armouring incident responders
item.description: I took the audience on a journey that showed them how to be confident, creative, and capable when an incident is assigned to them. We showcased incident support structures like procedures, guidelines, and checklists, examining which ones work, which don't, and why. We also encouraged attendees to build their own and validate their effectiveness. Finally, we helped them identify focal points for getting the information they need, when they need it, so they can navigate this high-stress job with professionalism, dignity, and grace.

item.title: Canada Security Collective Calgary: Women in Leadership — Leading with Impact
item.description: Hosted a panel at CSC Calgary 2026 featuring female leaders from security, energy, and entrepreneurship. The discussion explored how leadership develops before a formal title appears, from leading authentically in male-dominated environments to navigating self-doubt and making pivotal decisions, and ended with a call to action for the security sector to better support future women leaders.
